title: Vibe Coding for Finance Teams: What It Is and How to Use It
summary: What vibe coding is, what it means for finance teams, where it helps and where it is risky, and the safer path for building finance workflows with AI.
body_markdown:
One of the biggest shifts in software is that you no longer need to know how to code to build with code. **Vibe coding** , the practice of building software by describing what you want in plain language and letting AI write it, has gone from a niche idea to the way a lot of software gets made. It is now reaching finance, where analysts and controllers are starting to "vibe code" their own tools and automations. This guide explains what vibe coding is, what it means for finance teams, where it helps, where it is risky, and the safer path for finance work.


## **What is vibe coding?**


Vibe coding is building software by describing the outcome you want to an AI in natural language, and letting the AI generate the code, rather than writing it yourself. The term, coined in the AI developer community, captures a new mode of building: you work by intent and iteration ("make it do this, now change that") rather than by writing every line. It has made software creation accessible to people who are not professional engineers, including finance professionals.


> Vibe coding moves the skill from writing code to knowing what to build. For finance, that is a profound shift, because the people who know what a finance tool should do are finance people, not engineers.


## **What vibe coding means for finance teams**


Finance teams run on a sprawl of spreadsheets, manual processes, and one-off tools, and they have always been blocked on engineering time to improve them. Vibe coding removes that block for a class of problems. A finance professional can now describe a tool or automation and get a working version without filing an engineering ticket:


- **Ad hoc analysis.** Spin up a script to clean, join, or analyze a dataset without waiting on data engineering.
- **Internal tools.** Build a small calculator, dashboard, or data-entry tool for the team.
- **Automations.** Wire up a repetitive task, pulling a report, reformatting data, sending a recurring summary.
- **Prototypes.** Mock up what a process or model could look like before asking for a real build.


This is part of the broader shift toward the[finance engineer](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/finance-engineer) , the finance professional who builds and operates systems rather than doing everything by hand. Vibe coding is one of the tools that makes that role possible.


## **Where vibe coding is risky for finance**


Here is the honest part. Vibe coding is powerful for prototypes and personal productivity, but finance is not a low-stakes domain, and vibe-coded tools carry real risks when they touch the numbers that matter:


- **Correctness.** AI-generated code can look right and be subtly wrong. In finance, a subtle error is a wrong number in a report or a filing.
- **No traceability.** A vibe-coded script often cannot show its work or tie its output back to source, which is exactly what finance needs to defend a number.
- **No controls.** One-off tools usually lack the approvals, access controls, and audit trail that governed finance work requires.
- **Maintenance and key-person risk.** A tool one person vibe-coded can break silently and may be unmaintainable when they leave.


The rule of thumb: vibe coding is great for exploration, prototypes, and personal tools, but the closer the work gets to the books, the financial statements, and anything an auditor will see, the more those risks matter.

For the high-stakes finance work, reconciliations, the close, forecasting, reporting, the answer is not raw vibe coding but the same ease of use with the controls finance requires. ## **How finance teams should approach vibe coding**


- **Use it to explore and prototype.** Vibe code analyses, mockups, and personal tools freely, this is where it shines.
- **Keep it away from the books unsupervised.** Do not let an ungoverned vibe-coded tool produce numbers that go to leadership, auditors, or filings without review.
- **Graduate high-stakes work to a governed platform.** When a workflow becomes recurring and consequential, move it to an agent platform with traceability and controls.
- **Always keep a human in the loop.** Review what the AI produces, whether it is a script or an agent's output.


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is vibe coding?**


Vibe coding is building software by describing what you want to an AI in plain language and letting it write the code, rather than writing it yourself. You work by intent and iteration, which makes software creation accessible to non-engineers, including finance professionals.


### **Can finance teams use vibe coding?**


Yes, and increasingly do, for ad hoc analysis, internal tools, automations, and prototypes. It removes the engineering bottleneck for a class of problems. But for high-stakes work that touches the books, raw vibe coding lacks the traceability and controls finance requires.


### **Is vibe coding safe for finance work?**


For prototypes and personal tools, yes. For work that produces numbers for leadership, auditors, or filings, raw vibe coding is risky, AI-generated code can be subtly wrong, usually is not traceable, and lacks controls. High-stakes finance work belongs on a governed agent platform instead.


### **What is the difference between vibe coding and an AI agent platform?**


Both let you work in plain language. Raw vibe coding produces code with no built-in traceability, controls, or validation. A governed agent platform runs finance workflows with every output traced to source, validated against evals, and approved by a human, giving finance the accessibility of vibe coding with the governance it requires.


## **The bottom line**


Vibe coding is a genuine breakthrough: it lets finance people build tools and automations by describing what they want, no engineering ticket required, and it is a key enabler of the finance engineer. But finance is high-stakes, and raw vibe coding lacks the traceability and controls the books demand. Use it to explore and prototype; run the work that matters on a governed agent platform.
